reason: The text depicts harmonious relations between Hebrew leaders and the people. All twelve tribes approach David willingly in Hebron, declaring 'we are your bone and your flesh' and expressing their support. The elders make a covenant with David and anoint him as king. Throughout the passage, David leads the people in successful military campaigns against the Philistines and in religious ceremonies (bringing the Ark of the Covenant) where the people participate enthusiastically and joyfully. David distributes provisions to all the people and blesses them. The only interpersonal friction shown is Michal's personal contempt for David, not antagonism from leaders toward the people. The text demonstrates cooperative leadership and popular support rather than antagonism.
